newsitem.title: GERMANY: Fresenius asks shareholders to authorise capital.
newsitem.headline: Fresenius asks shareholders to authorise capital.

text.p: German medical products group Fresenius AG on Thursday asked its shareholders to authorise more capital to help prepare the group for further expansion.

"To strengthen our capital, after a capital rise in the spring, we asked shareholders to approve the creation of authorised capital of up to a nominal 30 million marks," management board chairman Gerd Krick said at the annual meeting.

Krick explained Fresenius, fresh from merging its dialysis unit with U.S. group National Medical Care into the world's biggest dialysis company, took this step to ensure it would be able to tap the capital markets as appropriate.
This spring Fresenius made a one-for-nine rights issue at 320 marks per nominal five-mark share earning the group 637 million marks, earmarked to support further expansion plans.
Krick also defended the group's 20 percent dividend increase even though shareholders complained about the payout.
"We think the dividend is appropriate," Krick said, commenting about Fresenius' decision to pay 1.90 marks per preference share and 1.80 marks per common share on 1996 earnings.
Similarly Krick defended the group's decision to fuse the dialysis business with National Medical Care, arguing this was the only way to ensure the group's competitiveness.
At the first ever annual meeting for Fresenius Medical Care, the dialysis unit in which Fresenius AG still holds a majority stake, Krick said FMC was eyeing more acquisitions.
